title: Changelog
content:
Notable package changes. This project follows Semantic Versioning.

See Project History for the reasoning behind each release.

1.1.0 - 2026-10-17

Added

Visible top-right developer dock with vector cheat/terminal icons, drag grip, safe-area clamping and retained position across visibility changes and screen resizing.

Cheat parameter forms generated from usage: required/optional fields, choice buttons, grouped coordinates, rest arguments, validation and retained input values. Run buttons assemble and execute commands without typing their names.

Category filters and per-card execution feedback, including errors. Terminal now has a Run button, Tab completion, keyboard history, command echo and a safe-area layout.

Local cheat-authoring skills under .agents/skills/cheat-terminal and .claude/skills/cheat-terminal.

Unity tests for command forms, quoted values, execution, UI interaction, dock dragging and pause restoration.

Changed

Default shortcuts are F1: Cheat Library, F2: Terminal. F10 remains a cheat shortcut; F9 toggles the dock; backquote opens Terminal; Escape closes the active surface. ConsoleKey and the new CheatHudKey are configurable.

Redesigned both surfaces with consistent dark colors, mint accents, clearer spacing and dedicated controls. Switching surfaces closes the previous one while retaining aggregate visibility/pause behavior.

Cheats run through explicit Run buttons; parameter forms are always visible. No additional registration is needed.

Previous release entries are numbered 1.0.0 through 1.0.4; this UI update is 1.1.0.

Fixed

Quoted argument serialization preserves spaces, embedded quotes, backslashes and empty quoted tokens.

HUD execution feedback reflects command errors instead of reporting every invocation as successful.

Generated dock icons and panel backgrounds include their required CanvasRenderer. Parameter fields retain their minimum height and no longer overlap Run buttons without a theme asset.

1.0.4 - 2026-08-29

Changed

The cheat HUD covers the whole screen instead of sliding in from the left. Rows are proper touch targets (104px minimum), content is inset by Screen.safeArea, wide screens split the list into two or three columns, and the bottom bar carries a large CLOSE button. The old panel is still available through TerminalBehaviour.CheatHudFullScreen = false and CheatHudView.WidthPercent.

Added

Open/close listeners: TerminalBehaviour.VisibilityChanged (console and HUD combined), ConsoleVisibilityChanged, CheatHudVisibilityChanged. The views raise OnOpened / OnClosed / OnVisibilityChanged directly.

TerminalBehaviour.PauseGameWhileOpen / PausedTimeScale: hold Time.timeScale while open and restore it on close.

Console keyboard shortcuts for the editor and desktop: F1 toggles, the backquote ` only opens (so it never eats a keystroke while typing). The cheat HUD also answers to F2 next to F10.

Tools > Cheat Terminal editor menu for play mode (toggle console / HUD / handle, Pause Game While Open, manual bootstrap).

TerminalShortcutKey gained F1-F4, F11, F12, BackQuote, Escape; MultiFingerTapGesture accepts a second AlternateKey.

Fixed

Input System-only projects had no EventSystem, leaving every console and cheat HUD button dead. One is now created with InputSystemUIInputModule.

Documentation

Added a Project History page reconstructed from the commit history (ko / en / ja / zh).

1.0.3 - 2026-08-17

Changed

The top-right >_ handle is hidden by default. Tapping with four fingers three times anywhere on screen shows it, and the same gesture hides it again. TerminalCornerTrigger.Visible / TerminalBehaviour.HandleVisible expose it from code (TerminalCornerTrigger.Enabled is kept as an alias).

Added

Cheat HUD (CheatHudView): a UI Toolkit panel that slides in from the left and lists every registered command, grouped by category. Toggled by tapping with three fingers three times (F10 on desktop) or through TerminalBehaviour.Open/Close/ToggleCheatHud(). Cheats without arguments run on a single tap; cheats with <...> or [...] arguments open an inline input. Includes a search box, a status line for the last executed command, and a >_ button that opens the console.

MultiFingerTapGesture: reusable "N fingers, M taps" detector that requires an exact finger count, so the three- and four-finger gestures never trigger each other. Optional keyboard fallback (F9 / F10) for the editor and desktop.

TerminalInput: reflection-free input abstraction covering both the legacy Input Manager and the Input System package.

AGENT.md documenting the conventions for authoring cheats.

1.0.2 - 2026-06-27

Changed (breaking)

Removed reflection-based [Terminal] method discovery and invocation. Commands are now registered explicitly with RegisterCommand(...).

Removed the reflection-based Object Inspector module from the default runtime.

EventSystem fallback no longer probes optional Input System types via reflection. Projects using Input System-only input should provide an EventSystem with InputSystemUIInputModule.

Fixed

Terminal input now executes only on an explicit submit, not on focus loss.

Terminal output escapes rich text-sensitive characters before wrapping lines in color tags.

Unity component commands now use invariant-culture numeric parsing, strict bool parsing, and inactive-inclusive GameObject lookup where appropriate.

Runtime helper GameObjects created by Logs and Performance modules are disposed with the terminal bootstrap.

Added

Cached completion items for command names, usage keywords, and command-specific providers.

Context-aware completions for built-in commands, including scenes, logs, GameObjects, component targets, and boolean values.

data [table] [id|text] command plus RegisterDataTable(...) for reflection-free data lookup.

Terminal UI tabs for Console, registered Commands, and registered Data tables.

1.0.1 - 2026-05-30

Changed

Renamed the namespace from UniTerminal to Achieve.CheatTerminal.

Added

Unity component commands: transform, rb, cam, light, audio, time, go.

Documentation in Korean, English, Japanese and Chinese, including advanced module usage.

1.0.0 - 2026-05-29

Changed (breaking)

Removed the internal collaborator interfaces (ICommandRegistry, ICommandParser, ICommandHistory, IAutoCompleteProvider, IAliasResolver, IArgumentConverter, ITerminalTrigger, ITerminal) and TerminalBuilder. The core Terminal is now a concrete class that owns concrete collaborators. Only ICommand, ICommandOutput, ITerminalView, and ITerminalModule remain as real extension points.

No marker interface for commands - the [Terminal] attribute is the only marker.

Terminal.ScanStaticCommands() scans user assemblies and auto-registers all static [Terminal] methods. The bootstrap runs it on startup through TerminalBehaviour.AutoScanStaticCommands. Instance commands still use Register(this).

Added

Runtime Logs module: captures Debug.Log output into a ring buffer with logs [n | error | warning | info | <text> | find <text> | clear | export]. Export writes to Application.persistentDataPath so logs are retrievable on device.

Up/Down arrow recalls previous/next command history in the input field via uGUI IMoveHandler, so it works under both the legacy Input Manager and the Input System package.

help <category> lists the commands in a category with descriptions. help now hints at help <command> / help <category>.

Fixed

EventSystem now creates InputSystemUIInputModule when the Input System package is active, resolved via reflection, avoiding the per-frame InvalidOperationException.

Top-right corner trigger is now a visible >_ handle and opens on a single tap.

0.1.0 - 2026-05-29

Added

Core command system: ICommandRegistry, ICommandParser (quote-aware), ICommandHistory, IAutoCompleteProvider, IAliasResolver, IArgumentConverter, and ICommandOutput with default implementations.

[Terminal("name {0}")] attribute and reflection-based AttributeCommand binding, including positional binding, optional parameters, and CommandContext injection.

Interface-driven Terminal core assembled via TerminalBuilder.

uGUI overlay view (UGuiTerminalView) deactivated while closed for zero idle cost.

Top-right corner open gesture (TerminalCornerTrigger, double-tap by default).

TerminalBehaviour bootstrap with a static convenience API. It auto-bootstraps in the editor and development builds.

Built-in commands: help, clear, history, echo, alias.

Module system (ITerminalModule) with InstallModule / GetModule<T> on the bootstrap.

Scene Tools module: scene list | load <name> [additive] | unload <name>.

Object Inspector module: find, inspect, set <name>.<member> <value>, call, with explicit object registration (ObjectInspectorModule.RegisterObject).

Performance Monitor module: perf (FPS, frame ms, memory, GC, render stats via ProfilerRecorder).

Basic Usage sample.

title: Getting Started
content:
Installation

In Unity Package Manager, choose Add package from git URL:

https://github.com/achieveonepark/cheat-terminal.git

Opening the console

The terminal bootstraps automatically in the editor and development builds. A developer dock is visible at the top right: the sliders icon opens Cheat Library and the terminal icon opens Terminal. Drag the grip or either icon to move the dock within the safe area.

// Release builds do not auto-create the console, so call this once.
Achieve.CheatTerminal.TerminalBehaviour.Bootstrap();

Action	How	Editor / desktop
Show / hide the top-right Terminal handle	Tap with 4 fingers, 3 times	F9
Open / close the cheat HUD	Tap with 3 fingers, 3 times	F1, F10
Open / close the console	Tap the Terminal handle, or the panel Close	F2, `
Run a command	Type and press Enter	
Previous / next history	Up / Down arrow	
Help	help, help <category>, help <command>

Repeating the same gesture closes it again. See Cheat HUD for details.

Using it in the editor

A mouse cannot produce a multi-touch gesture, so the editor and desktop use keys instead:
F1 opens Cheat Library, F2 opens Terminal, F10 is another cheat shortcut, and F9 toggles the dock. Backquote only opens Terminal; Escape closes the active surface.

When the Game view does not have focus the keys never reach the game. Use the menu then:

Tools > Cheat Terminal > Toggle Console
                       > Toggle Cheat HUD
                       > Toggle Corner Handle
                       > Pause Game While Open

Nothing is clickable without an EventSystem. If the scene has none, the terminal creates
one - with InputSystemUIInputModule in Input System-only projects.

Control from code

using Achieve.CheatTerminal;

TerminalBehaviour.Open();        // Open
TerminalBehaviour.Toggle();      // Toggle
TerminalBehaviour.Execute("gold 100000"); // Execute directly

TerminalBehaviour.ToggleCheatHud();      // Toggle the cheat HUD
TerminalBehaviour.HandleVisible = true;  // Show the top-right handle

// Open / close listener (console and cheat HUD combined)
TerminalBehaviour.VisibilityChanged += open => Time.timeScale = open ? 0.2f : 1f;
TerminalBehaviour.PauseGameWhileOpen = true; // the same thing, in one line

Parameter forms and execution

Parameter fields are always visible. Enter values and press Run or Enter; you never need to type the command name. <amount> is required, [amount] is optional, <x> <y> <z> creates separate coordinate fields, and <on|off> adds choice buttons. Required fields must be filled. Optional fields can be omitted from the end, without gaps. [args] and <text...> accept several space-separated arguments; quote a single value that contains spaces.

Use category buttons and search to find commands. Values survive filtering, resizing and reopening. Results and errors appear on the card, bottom status bar and terminal output. Switching surfaces closes the previous surface.

Next: Adding Commands

title: Project History
content:
How this package evolved, reconstructed from its commit history. The
Changelog records what changed in each release; this page records why.

At a glance

Version	Date	Headline change
1.1.0	2026-10-17	Parameter forms, draggable dock, F1/F2 shortcuts and execution feedback
1.0.4	2026-08-29	Full-screen cheat HUD, visibility events and editor support
1.0.3	2026-08-17	Multi-touch gestures bring the UI up; UI Toolkit cheat HUD
1.0.2	2026-06-27	Reflection removed for good, context-aware completion, data tables
1.0.1	2026-05-30	Achieve.CheatTerminal namespace, Unity component commands
1.0.0	2026-05-29	Rewritten around a concrete core, Logs module
0.1.0	2026-05-29	First core, uGUI view, module system

Three turning points

Reflection → explicit registration. 0.1.0 discovered commands through a
[Terminal("name {0}")] attribute and reflection binding, and 1.0.0 added automatic
scanning of static methods on top. To keep runtime behavior predictable under IL2CPP/AOT,
1.0.2 removed the attribute, the scan and every reflective call path, leaving explicit
RegisterCommand(...) as the only way in.

Interface zoo → concrete core. The collaborator interfaces of 0.1.0
(ICommandRegistry, ICommandParser, IAutoCompleteProvider, …) and TerminalBuilder
were deleted in 1.0.0; Terminal now owns concrete collaborators directly. Only
ICommand, ICommandOutput, ITerminalView and ITerminalModule remain as extension
points.

Always-on UI → gesture-summoned UI. The invisible double-tap corner area of 0.1.0
became a visible single-tap >_ handle in 1.0.0, and in 1.0.3 that handle itself became
hidden by default, reachable only through a multi-touch gesture.

1.0.3 — Gestures and the cheat HUD

The top-right >_ handle is hidden by default; four fingers tapped three times shows
and hides it.

Added a UI Toolkit cheat HUD that slides in from the left. Every registered command is
listed automatically, grouped by category, and cheats without arguments run on a single tap.
Three fingers tapped three times opens and closes it. → Cheat HUD

Gestures come from MultiFingerTapGesture, which requires an exact finger count so the
three- and four-finger gestures can never trigger each other.

Touch reading goes through the TerminalInput abstraction, covering the legacy Input
Manager and the Input System package without reflection (the latter being an optional
dependency resolved by a version define).

Added AGENT.md at the repository root with the conventions for authoring cheats.

1.0.2 — Reflection removed, completion sharpened

Deleted TerminalAttribute, AttributeCommand and the reflection-based Object Inspector
module. Commands previously registered through the attribute must move to
RegisterCommand(...).

Completion now caches command names, usage keywords and command-specific candidates, and
offers context-aware suggestions for scenes, logs, GameObjects, component targets and
boolean values (ICommandCompletionProvider, CommandCompletionContext, CompletionItem).

RegisterDataTable(...) and the data [table] [id|text] command expose game data tables
without reflection.

The terminal UI gained Console / Commands / Data tabs.

Fixes: input runs only on an explicit submit rather than on focus loss, output escapes rich
text-sensitive characters, Unity component commands parse with invariant culture, and the
helper GameObjects created by the Logs and Performance modules are disposed with the
bootstrap.

Around the same time the documentation site moved from Docusaurus to Fumadocs + Next.js,
the folder was unified as docs~, the Introduction / Getting started / Usage / Changelog
structure was settled and a Korean CHANGELOG.ko.md was added.

1.0.1 — Namespace and Unity component commands

Renamed the namespace UniTerminal → Achieve.CheatTerminal (breaking).

Added commands that drive Unity's built-in components directly: transform, rb, cam,
light, audio, time, go. → Unity component commands

Localized the docs into ko / en / ja / zh, added the advanced ITerminalModule section and
introduced the CHANGELOG.

1.0.0 — Rewritten around a concrete core

Removed the collaborator interfaces and TerminalBuilder; Terminal became a concrete class.

Terminal.ScanStaticCommands() auto-registered static [Terminal] methods (this was later
removed in 1.0.2).

Runtime Logs module: captures Debug.Log into a ring buffer, queried with
logs [n | error | warning | info | <text> | find <text> | clear | export]. export writes
to Application.persistentDataPath, so logs are retrievable from a device.

Up/Down arrows recall command history in the input field, and help <category> was added.

Fixed the EventSystem input module, turned the corner trigger into a visible >_ handle with
a single tap, added Unity .meta files, and settled the package name
com.achieve.cheat-terminal.

Added the documentation site (Docusaurus) and CI that deploys it to GitHub Pages.

0.1.0 — First release

Core made of a quote-aware parser, history, aliases, argument conversion, completion and an
output buffer.

[Terminal] attribute binding through reflection, assembled with TerminalBuilder.

uGUI overlay view that is fully deactivated while closed, plus a double-tap corner trigger.

Built-in commands help, clear, history, echo, alias.

Module system (ITerminalModule) with Scene Tools, Object Inspector and Performance modules,
and the Basic Usage sample.

Upgrade cheat sheet

Was	Is
[Terminal] attribute / static scan	TerminalBehaviour.RegisterCommand(...)
UniTerminal namespace	Achieve.CheatTerminal
TerminalBuilder assembly	new Terminal() + AttachView(...)
Object Inspector module	RegisterDataTable(...) + the data command
Always-visible corner handle	Four-finger triple tap (TerminalBehaviour.HandleVisible)
TerminalCornerTrigger.Enabled	TerminalCornerTrigger.Visible (Enabled kept as an alias)

title: Introduction
content:
Cheat Terminal is a Unity runtime developer console for cheats, debugging, log review, and live runtime control.

Commands are registered explicitly with RegisterCommand(...). There is no automatic assembly scanning or reflection invocation in the default runtime path, which keeps IL2CPP/AOT builds predictable. The console runs as a uGUI overlay with zero idle cost while closed.

TerminalBehaviour.RegisterCommand(
    "gold",
    ctx => ctx.Output.WriteLine("gold added", LogLevel.Success),
    "Add gold",
    "Cheats",
    "gold <amount>");

Features

Explicit registration - Register commands with RegisterCommand("name", ctx => ...); no hidden reflection scan.

Runtime IntelliSense - Shows command, keyword, data table, and row suggestions with details.

Performance-first - Disabled canvas while closed, capped output ring buffer, and keyboard history through the shared TerminalInput backend.

Modular - Scene, Data, Performance, Logs, and Unity Components modules are installed by default.

Tabbed UI - Console, Commands, and Data tabs show output, registered commands, and registered data.

Mobile-friendly - Multi-touch gestures (3 or 4 fingers, tapped 3 times) bring the UI up, and device logs export to a file.

Cheat HUD - Run registered cheats with parameter fields and Run buttons in a full-screen UI Toolkit panel; open/close listeners drive Time.timeScale.

Requirements

Unity 6 (6000.x)

com.unity.ugui (included by default)

Next: Getting Started

title: Adding Commands
Cheat HUD
content:
Every cheat registered on the terminal can be run from a full-screen UI Toolkit HUD.
Registering a command is all it takes: the HUD picks it up automatically.

Opening it

Gesture	Action	Editor / desktop
Tap with 3 fingers, 3 times	Open / close the cheat HUD	F1 / F10
Tap with 4 fingers, 3 times	Show / hide the top-right Terminal / F2 handle	F9
Tap the handle	Open / close the console	F2 / `

In the editor the Tools > Cheat Terminal menu does the same thing - use it when the Game view
does not have focus and the keys never reach the game.

using Achieve.CheatTerminal;

TerminalBehaviour.OpenCheatHud();
TerminalBehaviour.CloseCheatHud();
TerminalBehaviour.ToggleCheatHud();

Layout

The HUD covers the whole screen by default. Every row is a comfortable touch target
(104px minimum) with text sized to match.

Content is padded by Screen.safeArea, so notches and home indicators never cover a row.

Wide screens (landscape, tablets, the editor Game view) split the list into two or three
columns automatically.

The bottom status bar carries a large CLOSE button, for when the X in the header is out
of thumb reach on a tall phone.

Prefer the old narrow panel that slides in from the left? Turn full screen off.

TerminalBehaviour.CheatHudFullScreen = false;           // back to the sliding panel
TerminalBehaviour.Instance.CheatHud.WidthPercent = 42f; // its width, in percent

Open / close listeners

The game keeps running behind the HUD and the console. Subscribe to the open/close state to
drop Time.timeScale, block input, or anything else.

// true when the console or the cheat HUD opens, false once both are closed
TerminalBehaviour.VisibilityChanged += open => Time.timeScale = open ? 0.2f : 1f;

// or one surface at a time
TerminalBehaviour.CheatHudVisibilityChanged += open => { /* ... */ };
TerminalBehaviour.ConsoleVisibilityChanged  += open => { /* ... */ };

If all you need is to stop time, it is one line. The time scale in effect when the HUD opens is
saved and restored on close.

TerminalBehaviour.PauseGameWhileOpen = true; // hold the time scale while open
TerminalBehaviour.PausedTimeScale = 0f;      // the value to hold (default 0)

Unsubscribe with -=. The views raise the same events directly:
CheatHudView.OnOpened / OnClosed / OnVisibilityChanged, and the identically named
events on UGuiTerminalView.

How entries are listed

Commands are grouped by category; the built-in System category is always sorted last.

The search box at the top filters by name, description and category.

The usage string decides how a cheat runs.

usage	HUD behavior
god (no arguments)	Press Run
gold <amount>	Enter amount, then Run
heal [amount]	Leave amount blank or enter it, then Run

// One-tap cheat: no <> or [] in the usage string.
TerminalBehaviour.RegisterCommand("god", ToggleGod, "Toggle god mode", "Cheats", "god");

// Cheat with arguments
TerminalBehaviour.RegisterCommand("gold", AddGold, "Add gold", "Cheats", "gold <amount>");

Behavior

The HUD subscribes to Terminal.Registry.Changed, so commands added or removed at runtime
show up right away.

Results go to the terminal console output and to the status line at the bottom of the HUD.

While closed the panel is display: none, so it costs nothing to render or lay out, and the
root element never intercepts gameplay input.

The Terminal / F2 button in the header opens the full terminal console.

Dock and shortcuts

The terminal bootstraps automatically in the editor and development builds. A developer dock is visible at the top right: the sliders icon opens Cheat Library and the terminal icon opens Terminal. Drag the grip or either icon to move the dock within the safe area.

F1 opens Cheat Library, F2 opens Terminal, F10 is another cheat shortcut, and F9 toggles the dock. Backquote only opens Terminal; Escape closes the active surface.

Parameter forms and execution

Parameter fields are always visible. Enter values and press Run or Enter; you never need to type the command name. <amount> is required, [amount] is optional, <x> <y> <z> creates separate coordinate fields, and <on|off> adds choice buttons. Required fields must be filled. Optional fields can be omitted from the end, without gaps. [args] and <text...> accept several space-separated arguments; quote a single value that contains spaces.

Use category buttons and search to find commands. Values survive filtering, resizing and reopening. Results and errors appear on the card, bottom status bar and terminal output. Switching surfaces closes the previous surface.

title: Command Reference
content:
Built-in commands

Command	Description
help [command|category]	Command list / details
clear	Clear output
history	Input history
echo <text>	Print text
alias <name> <expansion>	Register an alias (alias remove <name>, alias to list)

Modules

The default bootstrap automatically installs these modules.

Scene

scene list                 # Loaded scenes + build setting scenes
scene load Lobby           # Single load
scene load InGame additive # Additive load
scene unload InGame

Data

Browse registered data table IDs and row names.

data                 # Table IDs / names / row counts
data items           # Row IDs / names in the items table
data items sword     # Search IDs, names, summaries and print fields

Performance

perf   # FPS / frame ms / memory / Mono / GC / draw calls, batches, triangles when available

Logs

Captures Debug.Log output into a capped ring buffer.

logs                 # Latest 30
logs 100             # Latest 100
logs error           # Level filter (error / warning / info)
logs network         # Text contains filter
logs find <text>     # Explicit search
logs clear           # Clear
logs export          # Save to file (persistentDataPath, retrievable from device)

Unity Components

Control Unity's built-in components directly from the terminal. See Unity Component Commands for the full reference.

Command	Description
transform	Read or write position, rotation, and scale
rb	Rigidbody property control
cam	Camera settings (FOV, background colour, etc.)
light	Light property control
audio	AudioListener volume, mute, and pause
time	Time.timeScale and fixedDeltaTime control
go	GameObject activation, tag, and listing

Aliases and macros

Create aliases for frequent command combinations:

alias rich gold 999999
rich            # -> gold 999999

title: Unity Component Commands
content:
UnityComponentsModule provides seven commands covering the most frequently used Unity built-in components, all controllable from the terminal without touching any code.
The module is installed automatically in editor and development builds — no extra setup required.

transform — Transform manipulation

transform get   <name>                   # Print position, rotation, and scale
transform pos   <name> [x y z]           # Get or set world position
transform rot   <name> [x y z]           # Get or set euler rotation
transform scale <name> [x y z]           # Get or set local scale
transform reset <name>                   # Reset position, rotation, and scale to identity

Examples

transform get   Player
transform pos   Player 0 1 0
transform rot   Enemy  0 90 0
transform scale Boss   2 2 2
transform reset Cube

Omitting the x y z arguments prints the current value without modifying it.

rb — Rigidbody control

rb get       <name>           # Print all Rigidbody properties
rb velocity  <name> [x y z]  # Get or set linear velocity
rb gravity   <name> [on|off] # Get or set useGravity
rb kinematic <name> [on|off] # Get or set isKinematic
rb mass      <name> [value]  # Get or set mass
rb drag      <name> [value]  # Get or set linear damping (drag)

Examples

rb get       Player
rb velocity  Player 0 10 0
rb gravity   Player off
rb kinematic Player on
rb mass      Boulder 50
rb drag      Ship 0.1

An error is shown when the target GameObject has no Rigidbody component.

cam — Camera settings

Always targets Camera.main unless otherwise noted.

cam list                          # List all cameras in the scene
cam fov  [value]                  # Get or set fieldOfView (1–179°)
cam bg   [r g b [a]]              # Get or set backgroundColor (0–1 range)
cam ortho [on|off]                # Toggle perspective / orthographic
cam size  [value]                 # Get or set orthographicSize
cam clip  [near far]              # Get or set near and far clip planes

Examples

cam list
cam fov 75
cam bg 0.1 0.1 0.2
cam ortho on
cam size 5
cam clip 0.01 1000

light — Light control

light list                        # List all Lights in the scene
light intensity <name> [value]    # Get or set intensity
light color     <name> [r g b]    # Get or set colour (0–1 range)
light range     <name> [value]    # Get or set range
light shadow    <name> [on|off]   # Toggle soft shadows on or off

Examples

light list
light intensity Sun 1.5
light color     Sun 1 0.9 0.8
light range     PointLight 10
light shadow    Sun off

audio — AudioListener control

Affects the global AudioListener.

audio volume [value]   # Get or set master volume (0–1)
audio mute   [on|off]  # Mute or unmute audio
audio pause            # Pause all audio
audio resume           # Resume all audio

Examples

audio volume 0.5
audio mute on
audio pause
audio resume

time — Time control

time get            # Print timeScale, fixedDeltaTime, time, frameCount
time scale [value]  # Get or set Time.timeScale (≥ 0)
time fixed [value]  # Get or set Time.fixedDeltaTime

Examples

time get
time scale 0.5     # Slow motion
time scale 0       # Pause
time scale 1       # Resume normal speed
time fixed 0.02    # 50 Hz physics updates

Pause with time scale 0, inspect state via the terminal, then resume with time scale 1.

go — GameObject utilities

go list   [tag]             # List GameObjects (up to 40, optional tag filter)
go active <name> <on|off>   # Call SetActive
go tag    <name> [tag]      # Get or set the tag

Examples

go list
go list Player              # Only objects tagged "Player"
go active Enemy on
go active Canvas off
go tag Player Untagged

go list shows at most 40 objects from FindObjectsByType.

Value format reference

Type	Accepted formats
float	1, 1.5, -0.3
bool	on / off / true / false / 1 / 0
Vector3 (x y z)	Space-separated: 0 1 0
Color (r g b)	Float 0–1: 1 0.5 0

Category

All commands belong to the Components category. Run help Components to list them.
